sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry (L1). A separate 3xFLAG-tagged alpha-4 construct (L2/L3, position unspecified) showed surface immunoreactivity and GABA-evoked currents comparable to untagged alpha-4 in HEK-293 cells co-transfected with beta2 and delta subunits.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the tag is inserted between mature residues 4 and 5 of the alpha-4 subunit. With the signal peptide spanning canonical residues 1–35, mature residue 4 maps to canonical position 39 (K) and mature residue 5 to canonical position 40 (E), confirmed by reading the numbered sequence. Position 39 lies deep within the large extracellular N-terminal domain (36–257), 219 residues from the TM1 boundary, providing ample steric room for a short epitope tag. L2/L3 (PMC3371167) corroborate that FLAG tagging of GABRA4 alpha-4 is surface-tolerated and electrophysiologically functional, but those clips name no residue and cannot ground a separate site. FLAG (DYKDDDDK) or HA (YPYDVPDYA) epitopes inserted between mature residues 4 and 5 of GABRA4 (alpha-4 subunit) in full-length, membrane-anchored constructs expressed in mammalian cells; total and cell-surface expression measured by flow cytometry. A second independent paper (PMC3371167, L2/L3) reports a 3xFLAG-tagged alpha-4 construct with confirmed surface immunoreactivity and electrophysiological GABA responses comparable to untagged alpha-4, but does not state the insertion position and therefore cannot ground an independent site.

sources.claim: FLAG (DYKDDDDK) or HA (YPYDVPDYA) epitopes were inserted between amino acids 4 and 5 of the mature GABA A receptor subunit subtypes as needed, so that subunit total and cell surface expression could be determined by flow cytometry.

literature_notes: L2 and L3 (both PMC3371167) describe a 3xFLAG-tagged GABRA4 alpha-4 subunit with confirmed surface display (anti-FLAG immunoreactivity) and preserved electrophysiological function (GABA responses comparable to untagged alpha-4 in HEK-293 cells). However, neither clip states the insertion position, and GABRA4 has three distinct extracellular regions (36–257, 307–317, 543–554), so topology_derived classification does not apply and no region is named. These clips therefore cannot ground an independent site but substantially increase confidence in the L1 site. The validation_level for the L1 site is conservatively set to surface_only because L1 itself only reports flow cytometry for surface expression; the functional preservation evidence from L2/L3 is from a construct whose position is unverified relative to L1.
